I'm making concept art for a cooperative board game called Stewards of the Long Voyage: Great Houses steward a vast generation ship; generations of leaders rise and retire. Style: RETRO SPACE — a 1950s pulp science-fiction paperback cover come to life. Gouache painting with flat colour and soft painted gradients, halftone-dot shading, chunky outlines, chrome highlights, rocket fins, atomic starbursts, ringed planets, mid-century modern interiors, a cheerful key light. People are sincere, not parody; the stakes are real. Palette: deep teal (#0F3A48), turquoise (#3AB0A8), tangerine (#E8603A), mustard gold (#F6C85A), cream (#FBEFD6), pink (#E88AA0), lime (#A8C860). Never put any text, letters, logos, borders or watermarks in the images.

Tall portrait image, exactly the layout of the attached guide. Repaint the guide as a finished, empty event card frame for this game, flat and straight-on like a printed card template. Keep every shape exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is: the rounded picture window at the top; the cream text panel below it; the thin chrome rule across the card (the tuck line); and the dark band at the bottom with its gold stage disc, two round icon sockets, a name bar and a text bar. The picture window stays flat empty dark teal; the panels, sockets and bars stay plain empty cream; the stage disc stays plain gold. Paint only the card around them: a deep-teal card with a fine halftone texture, slim brushed-chrome bezels, a small tangerine hazard-stripe accent at both ends of the tuck line, and a faint atomic starburst in the dark band's corners. Calm and clear: this card mostly shows only its bottom band. No text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.

Wide landscape image, exactly the layout of the attached guide, filling the frame edge to edge. Repaint the guide as a finished house player board for this game, flat and straight-on like a printed board-game mat. The tall banner on the left is the house's identity and the hero of the board: paint it as a heraldic hanging banner in the house colour with a bold, simple emblem centred on it, readable from across a table: a lightning bolt striking through a cog, crackling sparks, electric blue. The emblem is graphic and iconic, in the 1950s atomic-age style, with chrome and gold accents, not a scene and with no people. Keep every other shape exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, and leave it empty for text: the name bar at the top, three growth cards, two tracks of round sockets on chrome rails, a wide panel bottom left and a narrow panel bottom right. Panels and sockets stay plain empty cream. Around them: a calm deep-teal board with a fine halftone texture, slim chrome bezels, a thin line of the house colour along the board edge, and nothing else. No people, no landscapes, no text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.
